items.followUp: Name the main stages of the cell cycle.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of the cell cycle.
rubric.description: The cell cycle is the sequence of events in which a cell grows and divides, from one division to the next.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the cycle of growth and division from one cell division to the next.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the cycle’s major parts.
rubric.description: The cell cycle consists of interphase and the cell-division phase.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming interphase and a part of the cell-division phase.

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the sequence of events in which a cell grows and divides, from one division to the next.
It consists of interphase (G1, S and G2) and the cell-division phase (mitosis and cytokinesis).

items.followUp: What is the role of oxygen in the electron transport chain?

rubric.why: Checks the direction and starting point of electron transfer.
rubric.description: Electron carriers pass electrons from NADH and FADH2 to oxygen, the final electron acceptor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing electron transfer from NADH or FADH2 to oxygen.

rubric.why: Checks an important outcome of electron transport.
rubric.description: The released energy helps build a proton gradient that drives ATP synthesis; oxygen is reduced to water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining ATP synthesis through the proton gradient or stating that oxygen forms water.

modelAnswer: In the inner mitochondrial membrane, electron carriers pass electrons from NADH and FADH2 to oxygen, the final electron acceptor.
The energy released helps build a proton gradient that drives ATP synthesis; oxygen combines with electrons and hydrogen ions to form water.

items.followUp: What happens to the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction when substrate concentration is increased beyond saturation?

rubric.why: Checks how rising substrate concentration leads to active-site binding.
rubric.description: As substrate concentration increases, more substrate molecules bind to enzyme active sites.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that increasing substrate concentration causes more substrate molecules to bind to enzymes.

rubric.why: Checks what happens when all enzyme active sites are in use.
rubric.description: When all active sites are occupied, the enzyme is saturated and the reaction rate is at its maximum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that all active sites become occupied or that the enzyme becomes saturated.

modelAnswer: As substrate concentration increases, more substrate molecules bind to enzyme active sites until all the active sites are occupied.
The enzyme is then saturated and the reaction rate is at its maximum; adding more substrate does not increase the rate.

items.followUp: Give one example of a plant organ that can act as a sink and later become a source.

rubric.why: Checks the distinction between a source and a sink.
rubric.description: A source produces and exports sugars; a sink uses or stores sugars.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly distinguishing a source from a sink.

rubric.why: Checks how a sink can later supply food to other plant parts.
rubric.description: A sink becomes a source when stored food is mobilised and exported to other parts of the plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that stored food is mobilised and exported, so the sink functions as a source.

modelAnswer: A source is a plant part, such as a mature leaf, that produces and exports sugars; a sink is a part that uses or stores sugars, such as a growing region or tuber.
A sink can become a source when stored food is mobilised and exported to other parts of the plant—for example, a tuber supplying food to new growth.

items.followUp: Explain how Biology is related to Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Computer Science.

rubric.why: Checks the relationship between Biology and Physics.
rubric.description: Biophysics applies principles of Physics to explain biological structures and processes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly explaining that biophysics applies Physics to biological structures or processes.

rubric.why: Checks the relationship between Biology and Chemistry.
rubric.description: Biochemistry studies the chemical substances and reactions occurring in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly explaining that biochemistry studies chemicals or chemical reactions in organisms.

rubric.why: Checks the relationship between Biology and Mathematics or Statistics.
rubric.description: Biometry uses mathematical and statistical methods to analyse biological data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly explaining that biometry uses mathematics or statistics to analyse biological data.

rubric.why: Checks the relationship between Biology and Computer Science.
rubric.description: Bioinformatics uses computers to store and analyse biological information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly explaining that bioinformatics uses computers to store or analyse biological information.

modelAnswer: Biophysics applies the principles of Physics to explain biological structures and processes.
Biochemistry studies the chemical substances and reactions occurring in living organisms.
Biometry uses mathematical and statistical methods to analyse biological data.
Bioinformatics uses computers to store and analyse biological information.
